newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES BEAT BRAVES 3-2 FOR 23RD WORLD SERIES TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES BEAT BRAVES 3-2 FOR 23RD WORLD SERIES TITLE.

text.p: Joe Girardi drove in the first run and scored another in a three-run third inning as the New York Yankees beat the Atlanta Braves 3-2 on Saturday to win their 23rd World Series championship.

Jimmy Key and four relievers outduelled four-time Cy Young Award winner Greg Maddux and closer Mark Wohlers as the Yankees completed a remarkable comeback in the best-of-seven series by sweeping three games in Atlanta and taking one at home after opening with two demoralising losses at Yankee Stadium.
No team had ever before lost the first two games at home and won the next three on the road.
The game was a pitching rematch of Game 2, won by Maddux 4-0.

Key in 5 1/3 innings yielded one run on five hits with three walks and a strikeout. David Weathers, Australian Graeme Lloyd, Mariano Rivera and John Wetteland combined to hold the Braves to just one more run the rest of the way.
Wetteland picked up his fourth save of the Series despite allowing three hits and a run in the ninth.
Maddux in 8 1/3 innings yielded three runs on eight hits with three strikeouts and a walk. He had just one bad inning as the Yanks scored all their runs in the bottom of the third.

Paul O'Neill led off with a double to the right-field corner and moved to third on Mariano Duncan's ground-out. Girardi then whacked the first pitch he saw to the wall on one hop for an RBI triple and the first run of the game.
Derek Jeter then hit a line single to left that made the score 2-0, and one out later Bernie Williams singled in Jeter for a 3-0 lead.

The Braves got on the board in the fourth when Fred McGriff drew a one-out walk and Javier Lopez and Andruw Jones singled to load the bases. Key then walked Jermaine Dye on a 3-1 pitch in the dirt and Atlanta had its first run.
But after a mound conference, with the bases still loaded, Key got designated hitter Terry Pendleton to ground into an inning-ending double play, quelling the threat.
The Braves fell just short in the ninth.

Ryan Klesko got an infield single off Wetteland's glove. Pendleton followed with an 0-2 single to right and men were on first and third with one away. Pinch-hitter Luis Polonia then struck out before Marquis Grissom singled to drive in Klesko and make it 3-2 with men on first and second.
But Wetteland got Mark Lemke, after fouling into the Atlanta dugout, to foul out to third baseman Charlie Hayes and the Yankees were champions again.
The celebrating Yankees threw themselves into one huge single pile on the mound as police, several dozen on horses, came on the field to protect them.
Wade Boggs rode off in triumph behind a policeman on one of the horses, waving to the crowd.

With their 23rd World Series championship and first since 1978, the Yankees equalled the National Hockey League's Montreal Canadiens as the North American sports franchise with the most championships.
The defending champion Braves have played in four of the last five World Series and lost three of them.
The Yankees won all eight of their post-season road games, the first time a team ever won more than five away from home.

The Braves had two runners thrown out at second base, the second, Grissom, on a controversial call that Atlanta manager Bobby Cox argued. He became the sixth manager ever ejected from a World Series game.
